name: Eliel
overview: Eliel was a male member of the tribe of Levi known primarily as the chief of the sons of Hebron. His leadership role is explicitly noted in 1 Chronicles 15:9, highlighting his position within the Levitical community. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliel means 'G-d is my G-d,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God (El). This proper name, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 15:9, emphasizes a personal acknowledgment of God's sovereignty.
familyAndRelationships: Eliel is identified as a descendant of Hebron, establishing his lineage within the Levitical family. Scripture does not record any further family relationships beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Eliel's significance lies in his leadership as chief of the sons of Hebron, a role that would have involved responsibility in the religious and communal life of Israel, especially within the Levitical order. His mention in the context of 1 Chronicles 15:9 situates him within the preparations for the transportation of the Ark of the Covenant, underscoring his part in honoring God through worship and service. His position reflects the faithful stewardship expected of those serving in God's house.
